facts.item: swelling on the right side of the face and neck
facts.text: I have a swelling spread over the right side of my face and neck.

facts.item: pain or other symptoms from the swelling
facts.text: It doesn't hurt or cause me any other symptoms.
Over the past 3 to 4 years I've had similar, smaller swellings that went away on their own.
I can't link the swellings to any injury.
I can't link them to meals.
I can't link them to any toothache.
I can't link them to any general symptoms either.
I have no trouble opening my mouth.

findings.name: examination of the facial swelling
findings.result: 7 × 3 cm firm, non-tender, mobile swelling extending from the midface to the right submandibular region and from the oral commissure to the anterior border of the masseter; overlying skin normal; no inflammatory signs.

findings.name: oral examination
findings.result: Normal mouth opening, no trismus; normal salivary duct flow; normal intraoral findings.

findings.name: fine-needle aspiration of the swelling
findings.result: Yellowish mucoid fluid; microscopy shows cystic macrophages in a mucoid background.

findings.name: ultrasonography of the swelling
findings.result: 7–9 mL of slightly echogenic fluid with irregular margins anterior to the right mandibular angle, with no calcifications.

findings.name: contrast-enhanced MRI of the face
findings.result: Well-defined, lobulated 5.5 × 4.5 × 2.5 cm cystic lesion, hypointense on T1-weighted and hyperintense on T2-weighted images, with thin peripheral enhancement and a few septations. It lies anterior to the right submandibular gland, lateral to the mylohyoid muscle, and extends over the masseter, without invasion of the parapharyngeal or sublingual spaces. Submandibular and parotid glands appear normal. No “tail sign” toward the sublingual gland.

gold.reasoning: 1. Infection was unlikely — “Absence of inflammatory signs and normal intraoral findings excluded chances of infection.” 2. Tumor of salivary origin was less likely — “The recurrent nature of the swelling … nullified the tumerous etiology.” 3. Vascular malformation was excluded by aspirate — “The clinical picture of aspirate reduced the probability of vascular anomaly … to a great extent.” 4. Salivary retention cyst (true cyst) versus extravasation was considered given high amylase, but lack of epithelial lining (not yet histologically confirmed) leaned toward extravasation — “Aspirate had high amylase content. This information was more suggestive of a salivary cause for the lesion.” 5. Plunging ranula (sublingual gland origin) was excluded by imaging — “The typical ‘tail sign’ of a plunging ranula was not seen.” 6. Localization to submandibular gland on MRI focused the diagnosis on a submandibular mucous extravasation phenomenon.

quotes.f001: diffuse swelling on the right side of his face and neck
quotes.f003: similar, smaller swellings over the past 3–4 years that would spontaneously regress
quotes.f004: could not relate episodes to trauma

f002: 'Asymptomatic' swelling is written as a denial of pain or other symptoms from the swelling; no specific symptom other than pain is denied.
f004: 'Could not relate episodes to trauma, meals, dental pain, or systemic symptoms': each is written as an absent link, not as a general denial of the symptom.

notes: Index visit: the outpatient presentation with the asymptomatic right facial and neck swelling (s001–s006), with the aspiration and imaging of that workup (s009–s014).

s008 mixes results and interpretation: the results (no inflammatory signs, normal intraoral findings) are kept in the swelling and oral examinations; 'argued against infection' is dropped as clinician reasoning.
'No trismus' is both an explicit negative (patient fact f008) and part of the oral examination (mouth opening normal); dysphagia and dyspnea are reported as absent symptoms.
